Beautify.summary: Shows an intersection, or another composed object type, as a single object type in the editor.
Beautify.description:
Maps every property of T to itself: the type does not change, the way the editor shows it does. The hover of Entity & { name: string } shows the intersection; the hover of Beautify<Entity & { name: string }> shows { id: number; name: string; }, every property in one list.

Optional and readonly properties keep their modifiers, and only the first level is flattened. A union is flattened member by member, which makes the result of RequireOne readable.

reading.title: Reading a composed type
reading.body: The hover of each type is in its comment.

AbstractConstructor.summary: The type of a class, abstract or not, whose instances are of type T.
AbstractConstructor.description: Any class whose instances are assignable to T fits, abstract classes included, whatever the parameters of its constructor. Since the class may be abstract, a value of this type cannot be called with new: it is a class to check with instanceof, to read static members from, or to extend in a mixin. To create instances, use Constructor, which accepts only concrete classes.

members.T: The type of the instances. Without it, any class fits.
members.Statics: The static members the class must have, as an object type: AbstractConstructor<Shape, { unit: string }> accepts only the classes with a static unit string. Without it, no static member is required.

abstractClasses.title: Accepting abstract classes
abstractClasses.body: A filter by class only needs instanceof, which works with abstract classes too: AbstractConstructor lets it accept them.

Constructor.summary: The type of a concrete class whose instances are of type T: a value that can be called with new.
Constructor.description:
Any non-abstract class whose instances are assignable to T fits. The parameters of its constructor are not checked: the type is new (...args: any[]) => T, so new type() compiles even for a class whose constructor needs arguments. For abstract classes, use AbstractConstructor.

@xaendar/core uses it wherever a class is a value: the host directives of @WebComponent, the target of @Query.

members.T: The type of the instances. Without it, any concrete class fits.
members.Statics: The static members the class must have, as an object type: Constructor<Plugin, { id: string }> accepts only the classes with a static id string. Without it, no static member is required.

creatingInstances.title: Creating instances of a class
creatingInstances.body: The function receives classes and creates their instances. Statics requires each class to declare a static id.

ContainsChar.summary: Resolves to true when a string literal type contains a given character, to false otherwise.
ContainsChar.description:
Compares the characters of String with Contains one at a time, at compile time. Contains is a single character, or a union of characters to look for any of them: a longer string is never equal to one character, so ContainsChar<'1.5', '1.'> is false.

Only literals are inspected: for string the result is false, and for a union of literals it is boolean when only some of them contain the character. PositiveInteger is built on it.

rejectingLiterals.title: Rejecting literals
rejectingLiterals.body: In a conditional type, it turns a literal containing the character into never: a parameter of that type rejects the literal at compile time.

ClassAccessorDecoratorValue.summary: The getter and the setter of the accessor a decorator is applied to: the first argument of an AccessorDecorator.
ClassAccessorDecoratorValue.description:
A decorator applied to an accessor field receives the original get and set of the field, which read and write its storage. ClassAccessorDecoratorValue describes them, with Field as the type of the value. It is the shape of ClassAccessorDecoratorTarget of TypeScript, with this typed as unknown.

Neither function is bound: call them with the instance as this, as in value.get.call(this), inside the replacement accessor returned by an AccessorDecorator.

originalSetter.title: Calling the original setter
originalSetter.body: The replacement set clamps the value, then stores it through the original setter, called on the instance.

AccessorDecorator.summary: The type of a standard decorator of an accessor field, the kind @Query of @xaendar/core returns.
AccessorDecorator.description:
A standard (TC39) decorator applied to an accessor field. It receives the original getter and setter of the field, as a ClassAccessorDecoratorValue, and the context TypeScript passes to accessor decorators. It returns the replacements, each optional: get and set take the place of the originals, init receives the initial value of the field and returns the value it starts with. Returning nothing keeps the field as it is.

@Query returns one, and the types of @Property and @Event are derived from it.

members.Class: The class declaring the accessor: the type of this in the returned get, set and init.
members.Value: The type of the accessor: what get returns and what set and init receive. The decorator applies only to accessors of this type.

writing.title: Writing an accessor decorator
writing.body: A factory returning an AccessorDecorator: the replacement init and set keep the value between two bounds.

ClassDecorator.summary: The type of a standard class decorator that receives the class and returns nothing, the kind @WebComponent of @xaendar/core returns.
ClassDecorator.description:
A standard (TC39) decorator applied to a class. It receives the class, as a Constructor of T, and the context TypeScript passes to class decorators. Its return type is void: it registers the class, stores metadata or adds initializers with context.addInitializer, rather than replacing it.

It applies only to concrete classes whose instances are assignable to T. @WebComponent and @Directive return one.

members.T: The type of the instances: the decorator applies only to the classes whose instances are assignable to it.
members.Statics: The static members the class must have, as an object type. The default accepts any class.

registering.title: Registering a class
registering.body: A factory whose decorator stores the class of a page under its path. A class whose instances are not HTMLElements is rejected.

FieldDecorator.summary: The type of a standard decorator of a class field, which returns the initializer of the field.
FieldDecorator.description:
A standard (TC39) decorator applied to a field that is not an accessor. The field has no value yet when the decorator runs, so it receives undefined and the context TypeScript passes to field decorators. It returns an initializer: a function receiving the value the field is declared with and returning the value it is initialized with. The standard also allows a field decorator to return nothing; this type does not.

The initializer runs once per instance, when the field is initialized: later assignments are not intercepted. To act on every write, decorate an accessor with an AccessorDecorator.

members.Field: The declared type of the field: what the initializer receives.
members.ReturnType: The type the initializer returns, Field by default. TypeScript requires it to be assignable to the type of the field: a narrower type is accepted, a different one makes the decorator inapplicable.

transforming.title: Transforming the initial value
transforming.body: The decorator trims the string the field is initialized with. A later assignment keeps its spaces.

MethodDecorator.summary: The type of a standard method decorator, which can replace the method with another of the same type.
MethodDecorator.description:
A standard (TC39) decorator applied to a method. It receives the method and the context TypeScript passes to method decorators, and returns a replacement of the same type, or nothing to keep the method.

Method extends Function of this package, not the global one: its default, (...args: any[]) => void, accepts any method.

members.Method: The type of the method, which the replacement must have too. A wide type, such as (...args: any[]) => unknown, makes the decorator apply to any method.

wrapping.title: Wrapping a method
wrapping.body: The replacement logs the call, then calls the original with the same this and the same arguments.

Dictionary.summary: An object whose keys are all optional, with values of one type.
Dictionary.description: A Record<Key, Value> with every key optional: an object may have any of the keys, or none, and reading one gives Value | undefined. With a union of literals as Key, the other keys are errors; with string, any key is allowed. Value defaults to string.

optionalKeys.title: Optional keys
optionalKeys.body: Any key may be missing, so any read may give undefined, and the type says so.

AsyncFunction.summary: A function type returning a promise, built from the tuple of its arguments and the type the promise resolves to.
AsyncFunction.description:
AsyncFunction<[id: number], User> is (id: number) => Promise<User>. Without type arguments it is (...args: any[]) => Promise<void>. Any function returning such a promise fits, async or not.

It is Function with the return type wrapped in a Promise and, like it, a conditional type on Arguments.

typing.title: Typing an async function
typing.body: The type gives the arrow function assigned to it the type of its argument and of its result.

Function.summary: A function type built from the tuple of its arguments and its return type.
Function.description:
Function<[id: number, name: string], boolean> is (id: number, name: string) => boolean. The arguments are a tuple, labels included, so they can come from another type, as Parameters<F>. Without type arguments it is (...args: any[]) => void, which any function fits.

Its name is the one of the global Function, which the import shadows in the module. The other function types of the package fix part of it: VoidFunction, AsyncFunction, NoArgsFunction.

It is a conditional type on Arguments, resolved only once Arguments is known: inside a generic function, where Arguments is a type parameter, an arrow function is not assignable to Function<Arguments, Result>.

building.title: Building function types
building.body: A comparator built from the tuple of its arguments, and a variant of fetch built from its parameters.

NoArgsAsyncFunction.summary: A function type taking no arguments and returning a promise of ReturnType.
NoArgsAsyncFunction.description: NoArgsAsyncFunction<User> is () => Promise<User>, such as a loader with nothing to receive. Without a type argument it is () => Promise<void>, the same as NoArgsAsyncVoidFunction. A function with required parameters does not fit it.

NoArgsFunction.summary: A function type taking no arguments and returning ReturnType.
NoArgsFunction.description: NoArgsFunction<number> is () => number: a getter passed as a callback, a factory, a value computed only when it is read. Without a type argument it is () => void, the same as NoArgsVoidFunction. A function with required parameters does not fit it.

NoArgsAsyncVoidFunction.summary: A function type taking no arguments and returning a promise that resolves to nothing.
NoArgsAsyncVoidFunction.description: () => Promise<void>: an asynchronous task run for its effects, such as saving or reloading something. It is NoArgsAsyncFunction without a type argument.

NoArgsVoidFunction.summary: A function type taking no arguments and returning nothing.
NoArgsVoidFunction.description: () => void: a callback run for its effects, such as a cleanup function. Since the return type is void, a function returning a value fits too, and its value is ignored. It is NoArgsFunction without a type argument.

VoidAsyncFunction.summary: A function type taking the arguments of a tuple and returning a promise that resolves to nothing.
VoidAsyncFunction.description: VoidAsyncFunction<[user: User]> is (user: User) => Promise<void>: an asynchronous callback run for its effects. Without a type argument it takes any arguments. It is AsyncFunction with its return type left to the default.

VoidFunction.summary: A function type taking the arguments of a tuple and returning nothing.
VoidFunction.description:
VoidFunction<[event: MouseEvent]> is (event: MouseEvent) => void: a listener, or a callback run for its effects. Without a type argument it takes any arguments. Since the return type is void, a function returning a value fits too.

The DOM library of TypeScript declares a global VoidFunction too, taking no arguments: the import shadows it in the module.

Mutable.summary: Removes readonly from every property of an object type.
Mutable.description: The opposite of Readonly<T>: the same properties, with the same types and the same optional modifiers, all writable. Only the first level changes: the properties of a nested object stay readonly. A readonly array or tuple type becomes a mutable one.

building.title: Building a read-only value
building.body: The function builds the totals in a mutable object and returns them with their read-only type: the code receiving them cannot change them.

PositiveInteger.summary: Resolves to a number literal type when it is an integer of zero or more, to never otherwise.
PositiveInteger.description:
Reads the number as a string and rejects it when it contains a - or a ., with ContainsChar: negative numbers and decimals become never. Zero is accepted: PositiveInteger<0> is 0.

As the type of a parameter, it rejects at compile time the literals that are not valid counts. Only literals are checked: for number the result is number. TupleOfLength checks its length with it, and the cursors of the compiler the number of characters their peek reads.

checkingACount.title: Checking a count
checkingACount.body: The type parameter captures the literal passed, and the parameter becomes never when the literal is not an integer of zero or more.

RequireOne.summary: Makes at least one of some keys of an object type required.
RequireOne.description:
The result is a union with one member per key of Keys: in each, that key is required and the other keys of Keys are optional. The keys outside Keys keep their modifiers. An object fits when at least one of the keys is set, to a value other than undefined.

It suits an object of options that are optional one by one, when an empty object makes no sense: a search by id, by email or by both. Its hover lists the Picks it is made of: wrapped in Beautify, it shows the union of object types.

members.Keys: The keys of which at least one is required, every key of T by default. A key that T already requires satisfies the condition alone, so when T has one, list the optional keys here: RequireOne<Search, 'id' | 'email'>.

requiringOne.title: Requiring one option
requiringOne.body: A query by id, by email or by both: an empty object does not compile.

TupleOfLength.summary: A tuple of Length elements, all of type TupleType.
TupleOfLength.description:
TupleOfLength<3, string> is [string, string, string]; TupleType defaults to number. The tuple is built one element at a time in Acc, a parameter to leave out, so the length is limited by the recursion of TypeScript: up to 999 elements.

Length goes through PositiveInteger: a negative or a decimal literal gives never, and 0 gives the empty tuple. With number, which is not a literal, the result is the empty tuple too.

fixedLength.title: Fixed-length results
fixedLength.body: A function returning exactly three numbers, destructured by position, and a type nesting two tuples.
